Immune-mediated neutrophilic skin disease causing bullae and necrotic ulcers; associated lymphoproliferative diseases are separate conditions.
Defining neurodevelopmental disease; skeletal deformities include clinodactyly in 3/3, and eyelid ptosis occurs in 3/5. Estimates derive from a small cohort.
Adipocytic sarcoma typically arising in deep soft tissues of the extremities; metastatic sites are not intrinsic organ involvement.
Urothelial neoplasm arising in the ureter, which belongs to the renal axis.
Congenital cystic malformation of distal pulmonary airways and lung tissue.
Defining vertebral and long-bone dysplasia with restricted joints; supplied CNS, ocular and palatal abnormalities lack evidence of frequency at or above 30%.
Infantile degeneration of the cerebral cortex; supplied information establishes no additional organ involvement.
Glutathione synthesis defect causes organic acid accumulation, acidosis and hemolytic anemia; neurologic injury affects roughly half of systemic cases.
Atherosclerotic obstruction directly damages arteries; hyperlipidemia and hypertension are risk factors rather than additional affected organs.
Sympathetic neuronal tumour; intestinal neural proliferation/polyposis is annotated at 30–79%. Nonspecific adrenal abnormalities do not establish endocrine dysfunction.
Macroglossia, abdominal wall defects and somatic overgrowth define the syndrome. Transient neonatal hypoglycemia and later tumour risks do not establish additional damage.
Glial tumour arising within the central nervous system.
Partial dysfunction of the third cranial nerve; impaired eye movements result from nerve palsy without intrinsic eye damage.
Severe developmental epileptic encephalopathy; joint contractures occur in 2/2 assessed patients. Apnea and bradycardia reflect autonomic dysfunction; optic atrophy is under 30%.
IRF1 immunodeficiency; pulmonary infections are separately diagnosed consequences. Cytopenias in 1/2 lack evidence of persistent intrinsic blood disease.
PSEN2-associated cortical neurodegeneration; cerebral amyloid angiopathy is a distinct disease, and vascular deposits alone do not establish functional damage.
Benign adipocytic tumour arising within a tendon sheath.
Tuberculous infection of the fallopian tube; reproductive anatomy has no organ axis, but the infectious mechanism applies.
Glycosylation disorder defined by neurologic dysfunction and hypogammaglobulinemia. Pooled hepatic enlargement, optic atrophy and hearing loss are each under 30%.
Defining intellectual disability and lacrimal failure occur in 5/5; esophageal achalasia, a named syndrome feature, occurs in 3/5.
Developmental malformation of the eye's anterior segment; extraocular findings are not established across this umbrella.
Lysosomal CTSC deficiency with defining keratoderma and destructive periodontitis; acroosteolysis and skeletal abnormalities occur in 30–79%. Recurrent infections are under 30%.
Meningeal tumour involving the cavernous venous sinus; both meningeal origin and defined venous occupation apply. Cranial nerve palsies do not establish intrinsic eye damage.
